answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil raids with a progressive registration toll backed by linkable device proofs. Each new identity shows a unique hardware attestation, and its opal fee rises with every earlier identity linked to the same operator, forming a steep cost ridge. One honest agent pays little; a hundred clones pay a hundred escalating fees whose total grows quadratically. A public plume of linked proofs keeps clusters auditable, so no operator hides earlier identities. Splitting into fakes costs far more than single entries, while newcomers barely notice.
